utterances.text: Because after Mr. Stanisic returned to Belgrade he decided that he did not wish to employ me any more, or, rather, there was a problem with the funding in the case, and Stanisic did not feel that he could privately fund my services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Mr. Wilson in his letter suggests otherwise. I'll read what he says: "I do -- I do not know the exact date, but around 2005 Mr. Karganovic telephone me and told me he had been fired, discharged, from the Stanisic team in a dispute with the client." Did you have a dispute with the client that led to your termination?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have a dispute with the client and I resigned. I was not fired. I have my letter of resignation which I sent to Mr. Knoops and he can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Now, the reason Mr. Wilson sent his letter to Mr. Petrov was because you had offered a proffer to testify in the Popovic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And he was sending the letter because he felt that you were about to disclose confidential information or had already disclosed confidential information to the Popovic Defence team concerning solicitor-client privileged information that took place in the Obrenovic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That was his perception, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. And prior to -- when was the first time you met with the Defence of the Beara team?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I had known them for a number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. But in terms of this proffer, when -- I know that it was written in 2008, but in one of the correspondences that you have filed you suggest it was about a year before that you had spoken to them about making a proffer. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but a year or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: So sometime in the fall of 2007?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Could be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And I suggest to you, sir, that in 2006 you had spoken to Mr. Wilson about working for the Beara team and he had said, you cannot do it. The client doesn't agree. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And the Beara team actually made an application to the Registry to speak permission, Mr. Wilson and his client objected, the Prosecution objected, and you were told no; yes?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And not withstanding knowing that confidentiality of the relationship with Mr. Obrenovic was an issue, a year later you went and spoke to the Beara team and revealed some confidences, did you not?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: No. The idea was not for me to reveal confidences, but to impress those aspects of the bargaining process where Mr. Obrenovic may have been exposed to undue pressure by the Prosecutor. In other words, my proffer was essentially to testify about what the Prosecutor did or said in relation to the accused and not to talk about confidential conversations or case planning between the accused and his lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: You -- you know that when Mr. Wilson sent this letter he had already seen your proffer, did he not?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. And I'll just read to you what he says in his letter: "Those proofing notes clearly set forth that Mr. Karganovic intends to violate his duty as a member of the Obrenovic Defence team to maintain the confidentiality of all communications within that team. He has indicated that he will do so by testifying as to his supposed recollections of such communications, including supposes statements by the accused Obrenovic to his Defence team." He was concerned enough to write this letter to stop you from violating those confidences; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes that's correct. He was concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: May I finish my answer, please. And his concern -- and it was precisely when I reconsidered the whole issue that I decided that I would be treading too close to a dangerous area and that it may not be possible to isolate those aspects that would not infringe on the client-attorney relationship that I decided to ask to be withdrawn as a witness and I did not go ahead and testify in that case. So I think that I should be given credit for acting with prudence rather than criticised for acting improperly because I did not in the end act improperly or run the danger of so acting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Let me put this to you: In Wilson's letter describes your proffer in the following terms: "Mr. Karganovic's description of the debriefing session -- debriefing process is inaccurate, greatly misleading, and filled with innuendo. It is not -- it is insulting not only to Mr. McCloskey but to ourselves, Mr. Obrenovic's attorneys. Both Mr. Slijepcevic and myself have been attorneys for many years, more than 40 in my own case. I was the chief federal Prosecutor in my federal district in the United States, a Judge for eight years, a US Army lawyer and a military Judge, and have been a Defence lawyer in the private practice of law for more than eight years. Mr. Slijeptovic --"

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Slijepcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: "-- has been an attorney for more than 34 years and was a Judge in Belgrade before being fired by Mr. Milosevic's regime for refusing to adhere to the party line." Those are his comments about your proffer and I suggest to you, sir, that you're prepared to say anything for Mr. Krajisnik, as you were prepared to say anything to support the Beara defence?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate these are Mr. Wilson's comments. I know Mr. Wilson. He is a honest person and I respect him. However, he has a stake in making sure that I do not discuss some of those things even in the very limited way that that discussion was projected, because it would adversely effect a plea bargain which in the capacity of lead counsel he was closely involved. So he has a motive in portraying what I had proposed to do but did not in the most negative possible light.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. Let's talk about motive. What is the Stichting Srebrenica Historical Project?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a non-governmental organisation which was founded here in The Hague with myself as its president which has the purpose of investigating crimes and victims on both sides of the conflict in the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And who funds it?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: It is funded by contributions. We receive logistical support from the government of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And did you hold a conference in Banja Luka on the 4th of October, 2008?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And the reportage for that conference suggests that again you were holding yourself out to be an American lawyer. Perhaps we can -- I'll just read you from a clip that attributes some comments to you. And I can bring it up if need be.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Here it is. There's a quote in -- in Politika web site, www.politika.rs about this conference. You organised this international symposium?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And you are attributed to have said the following: "It is correct that a major number of captured Bosniaks had been executed in Srebrenica and that constitutes a major war crime. However, there is not a single piece of evidence that the crime had been committed pursuant to an order by the civil or military leadership of Republika Srpska. Moreover, there is no evidence that over 8.000 Bosniaks had been killed in Srebrenica as much as the number of Bosniak victims has been increased so have the Serb victims in this territory been reduced not to say underestimated." Stated the American lawyer Stefan Karganovic, president of the historical Serb project Srebrenica. Are those your words?

utterances.speaker: MR. N. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. The introduction to this whole statement was saying you are quoted as saying you are an American lawyer, and the quote has nothing no there to say that the witness said he is an American lawyer. So the whole premise of the question is invalid and I move that it be stricken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Dershowitz, I have started having some problems with your inventions because you're supposed to be a JCE counsel, and you are taking -- intervening on everything. A line of questions will go to the credibility of the witness, so I don't think it's appropriate you're doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Just two --

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Are those your words?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: The words that you quoted for the most part are my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: And they express my sentiments whether I quite put it that way or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the other part of it is concern, I would just like to point out that a graduate of the school of the geology is a geologist. A graduate of the school of accounting is an accountant. I should think that a graduate of a school of law would be a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Now let's just deal with your -- your current relationship with Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: You're currently helping him with his appeal in various capacities as interpreter, translator, as legal researcher, fact-finder, et cetera. And are you being remunerated for that assistance?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And how long have you been working with him on his appeal?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I have been assisting him virtually since shortly after the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. And how would you describe this in terms of occupation of time, full time, part time?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it varies from one period of time to another, but there were times when it was pretty much full time as, for example, when Mr. Nicholls was involved for a couple of months. It was a great deal of work. And of course I also had to translate and summarise large portions of the judgement before he actually received it late in 2007, and that took an enormous amount of time and effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you perform some services for Mr. Nicholls, is that fair?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And you were retained to -- or part of the Colin Nicholls Defence team from the 15th of December, 2006, I believe, to the 24th of April, 2006?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I was [Overlapping speakers] a member of Mr. Nicholls team. I worked with Mr. Nicholls, it being understood that I was assisting Mr. Krajisnik, and I was working with Mr. Nicholls with Mr. Krajisnik's knowledge and approval.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note would the witness kindly be asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Karganovic, could you speak into the microphone. The interpreters are having some difficulties.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I work with -- well, my answer appears here, so I think we're all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: So when you were working, and I'll use are words, I'll get to it later, when you were working with Mr. Nicholls, you were also working with Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And Mr. Nicholls was aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And when you became part of -- or when you started to assist Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Nicholls expressly advised you, did he not, that the only confidential communication that would take place between he -- or that is written or otherwise between he and the client would be material coming from him and not from anyone else who is working for Mr. Krajisnik, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And -- and it's my understanding that during the course of your working with Mr. Nicholls that you put into the confidential envelopes that he was sending to Mr. Krajisnik material other than he had seen or authorised, is that fair?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That is fair and I would like to explain that if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Just answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: You did that; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And when Mr. Nicholls found out about your actions he terminated your services immediately, did he not?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. And you continued to work for Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And at some point when explaining this to the Registry, you said that your -- you felt that even though you were working with Mr. Nicholls and you were being paid by the Registry to work with Mr. Nicholls, your accountability and your loyalty was to Mr. Krajisnik first; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly I regarded myself as an assistant to Mr. Krajisnik. Mr. Krajisnik, during that period, with all due respect for Mr. Nicholls, emphasised every single time that we went to see him, Mr. Nicholls and I, that he wanted to represent himself, that he did not want Mr. Nicholls to represent him or to write his appeal, and that he was unhappy with the situation that he perceived of Mr. Nicholls being imposed. My role in that interaction between the two of them was as an interpreter. It was mostly confined to going to the Detention Unit with Mr. Nicholls. The other part of what I was doing was to translate for Mr. Nicholls and for the benefit of Mr. Krajisnik some materials that Mr. Nicholls had sent me. So it was both translating and interpreting; and I was paid by the Registry, you are correct there, but not as a member of Mr. Nicholls' team because I was never formally appointed a member of his team. I was paid simply in my capacity as an interpreter and translator. I did the same kind of work in other cases without being a member of that team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. Certainly Mr. Nicholls thought you were part of the team because he terminated your services.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it struck me as very odd that he -- that it should occur to me -- to him to terminate me when I was not aware and I had no reason to think that he considered me his employee. And if you read the letter that I sent to him on that occasion, I think that you will clearly see that. You will see my perception of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: In any event you were suspended on the 24th of April 2007. On the 25th of April did you have communication with Mr. Nicholls on behalf of Mr. Krajisnik, telling Mr. Nicholls that Mr. Krajisnik no longer wanted to receive any communication from him?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that I sent him an e-mail to that effect, and it would have been at the request of Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you'll agree with me that in the September 3rd, 2007 letter that Mr. Petrov sent to you that Mr. Petrov disagrees with your interpretation that you were not part of the Colin Nicholls Defence team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see the letter in front of me, but I certainly recall it and I certainly do recall that Mr. Petrov did not share my view on that particular point, but I want to re-emphasise that in this institution, to the best of my knowledge; and I've been here for about five or six years, when someone is a member of a team, when one is -- when one becomes a member of a team a letter of appointment is issued to that effect. I never received one in relation to Mr. Nicholls and his team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And in any event, Mr. Petrov in his letter said, "Your statement that you were never a member of Mr. Nicholls' Defence team is inaccurate regardless of the fact that Mr. Nicholls may have only used your services on an ad hoc basis," correct? That's his position?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That's his position. I respect Mr. Petrov, but I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: In your letter of the 29th of June 2007 which is attached to a filing by Mr. Krajisnik, it's a letter in respect of the allegations about misuse of the improper procedure, you make some suggestions that Mr. Nicholls did not give you proper instructions about the use of the confidential envelope. I gather from your answer this afternoon that you agree that you did received instructions on the use of the confidential envelope and that your placing additional materials into the confidential envelope was never approved by Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it would be helpful if these materials that you refer to were introduced into the evidence so that the Chamber could read them and draw their own conclusions instead of just reading excerpts, because in my response to Mr. Petrov, I point out that even though technically that procedure may have been for the purpose of material to be passed from counsel to client, everything that I passed on to Mr. Krajisnik using that procedure was case related. It was material of the type that we have discussed a little bit earlier while I was translating for Mr. Krajisnik sections of the judgement and doing transcript research. So there was no private communication there whatsoever. That's point number one. And point number two, on several occasions when Mr. Nicholls and I went to see Mr. Krajisnik at the Detention Unit, I had passed similar material by hand to Mr. Krajisnik in Mr. Nicholls' presence, and Mr. Nicholls did not object. So my interpretation of his failure to object was that it was a functional endorsement. He did not ask to review the material to see what it was. He took it on faith as in fact was the case that it was all case related. I realise --

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I'm going to invite the Chamber to look at the material that Mr. Petrov forwarded to me. This witness is using considerable amounts of time rambling on.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And Mr. Petrov has decided in his letter quite clearly after a diligent investigation what he thinks the position is, and I'll leave it to the Chamber to decide on this question.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that is best, but I -- I object to your calling my answer rambling because I'm not rambling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. We will disagree over how we describe it.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Fine I can also disagree with some of the positions or interpretation that Mr. Petrov has taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Let's go to your letter of October 16, 2007.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Paragraph 9, and that's the only one I'm going to deal with and then I'm done: "It seems the Defence team did not have a plan according to which it operated particularly in the phase when the Defence started to present its evidence and no longer just reacted to some moves of the Prosecution. The approach was more often than not experimental rather than functionally directed," and then you give one example. "For instance, for some time we discussed about whether or not to open the issue of Muslim armament for which the accused had collected a lot of evidence in order to prove that the Serbian side was not an unprovoked aggressor in BH and, rather, reacted to other threats and provocations. Without any particular reason or explanation simply Stewart put this project ad acta and there was no presentation on evidence on this matter." Do you under oath accept that statement that there was no statement of Muslim army in the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I think that you're reading into that passage perhaps what you prefer to read into it. This is very specific. We are talking about a very specific project within the Defence team at this time to create a dossier on Muslim arming that would target that issue in a -- in an elaborate way, not just a few questions being put to this or that witness but something that would deal with the issue in a systematic way. That's what I'm referring to here. And under oath I can state that's exactly the way it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: So you won't disagree with me when I suggest to you that there was considerable cross-examination on the Muslim armament issue of Prosecution witnesses? I refer to the witness Deronjic, Ramic, Hasanovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I won't disagree with you, but that is a completely different kind of approach than the one that I'm talking about here. Haphazard rather than systematic in the course of the presentation of defence evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And during the course of defence evidence there was evidence led of Muslim disarmament -- or armament is that not right through the witness of Savkic, through the evidence of Bjelica; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, but here we're talking about a systematic presentation of that topic, not a few unrelated haphazard questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And in respect to the witnesses, let's just talk about the numbers. You mentioned that several witnesses were unable to travel and couldn't testify. A number were unwilling to testify. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Some were afraid, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Some witnesses perhaps didn't give you sort of the detail that was required to mount the kind of sophisticated defence that was perhaps being -- was under consideration?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not the judge of the adequacy of that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: That was for the lawyer, was it not, or the lawyers?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That was for Mr. Stewart to decide on the final analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: With Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Or Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I'm not sure when the Court wants to take a break. I think I'm close to my limit of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: You have around five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I wondered if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: And we won't take a break if you finish in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I wonder if I just consult with my colleagues if there's anything they can think of. If I could just have a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Just -- just a couple of questions to conclude. I'm looking at a -- a list of Defence witnesses that were called, and you will agree with me that the Trial Chamber gave the Defence a limited number of hours in which it could produce its defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And decisions had to be made in regard to who to call and for how long.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And Mr. Krajisnik had formed the opinion from before the Defence case even started that he was going to testify; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: No? Okay. Mr. Krajisnik did decide to testify at some point?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. And his testimony lasted about 40 court days.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And that consumed a large part of the time that was allocated to the Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And in my earlier testimony I said exactly what you're saying now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All right. And from reviewing just generally what the witnesses are talking about, there's a wide range of witnesses that talk about the politics before the war and even during the war. There are witnesses that talk about the political negotiations involved -- involving Mr. Krajisnik and others of the RS government; correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: There are representative witnesses from municipalities, from the SDS Main Board, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: All commenting on various issues that have been identified as important to Mr. Krajisnik's defence; right?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Comments may have been made on most of the important issues, but arguably what was absent was systematic and concerted treatment of many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: So you disagreed with, I guess -- the number of witnesses called could have been greater, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not arguing with the number. I would be more inclined to argue with the nature of the quality of some of the witnesses. And again, if I may unworthily elevate myself to the hypothetical position to which the distinguished Judge placed me, I probably would have excluded some of the witnesses and included some of -- some that I felt were more important or more pertinent to key issues, but that is a subjective judgement of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that you weren't there for the whole defence?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, but I'm talking about the period when I was there, which was when most of the witnesses if not -- well, most of them testified while I was there. I was not there while Mr. Krajisnik was testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And you were not there when most of the Prosecution witnesses were testifying?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And so that there is a large part of the case that you're missing, and that influences your ability to offer any opinion on what should have been done by the counsel who had been there from the beginning and finished the trial to its conclusion, is that -- or saw it to its conclusion?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, please, give me a break. I'm a literate person. I know how to look things up. Just because I missed a part of some event it doesn't mean that I cannot catch up. I -- of course, being personally there is a huge advantage. That doesn't mean that I cannot find out what went on in my absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: How did you find out by asking other people?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Well you can do that. You can go to the internet page and look up testimony that you thought might be interesting. There are many ways, very simple ways to find out and catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: But you were in court as a case manager, you were in court for the full period?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: And you weren't able to do any trolling through the record as it were?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to use a negative word about your question, but it is a bit tendentious because court is five hours. You have duties outside of court, and then you still have some time over the weekend and in the evening that you can use anyway you want. I'm not saying that I was perusing previous witness testimony. The only point that I'm making is that there are various ways of becoming informed about what went on before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yeah. But when you were working for the approximately 13 months as the case manager, interpreter, translator for the Krajisnik team, you had a full-time job.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I had a full-time job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: That doesn't exclude doing other things when the job is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Shahabuddeen, you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Just one -- just one question, Mr. Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Sorry. It concerns the testimony which Mr. Krajisnik gave over 40 days. Now, who examined Mr. Krajisnik for those 40 days?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was both Mr. Stewart and Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And then the time would come when Mr. Krajisnik would be re-examined. Who would have re-examined him?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: On any specific occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: During those 40 days of testimony --

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- a time would have come when he would have been re-examined by counsel. Which counsel?

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Your Honour, if the purpose of your question was -- is to find out whether I was keeping up with Mr. Krajisnik's testimony after I left the team, as I mentioned, shortly thereafter my mother, my cousin and I went to Serbia. So I was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So you are not in a position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not. No I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STEFAN KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not following it that closely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, this concludes the testimony of Mr. Karganovic. We thank you. You can -- you may be excused, and the usher would lead you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I would like to -- sorry, we can certainly move into open session now. Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before we adjourn, I was saying, I will have announce the decision of the Appeals Chamber as concerns the request filed by Mr. Krajisnik as concerns the statement of Radovan Karadzic. The Appeals Chamber has decided that under Rule 92 ter, the statement as annexed to the request should be admitted into evidence at the proceedings to be held on November 5, 2008, provided, of course, that the requirements set forth in Rule 92 ter are met, that is that Mr. Karadzic is present and is available for cross-examination and other questioning and will attest that the written statement reflects his declaration. There is a partial modification of the Scheduling Order of October 21. The hearing will start at 9.00 and not at 8.30. This being said, I think we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I just have a question in terms of the schedule for Wednesday. How much time will the Prosecution have to cross-examine? When will we start to cross-examine? I think it's important to know whether we have three hours, six hours, or nine hours. The other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: The other question I have and relates to today's hearing, I note that the Scheduling Order has an impact summary required for the 14th of November on the Karadzic testimony, but there was no order allowing impact submissions on the testimony today, and I'm just inquiring whether that was an oversight or wasn't intended to have submissions made regarding the testimony today. And then there's also a word limit. There's none prescribed in the order, and perhaps some direction as to how long the submissions should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, on the last question we have to go back to private session, but on the -- on the scheduling for Wednesday, the hearing will be like follows: There will be -- of course we will have to ascertain of course the conditions of 92 ter, and that would be the beginning the hearing. Then as of when this is done, the Appeals Chamber decided that the cross-examination by the Prosecution should take one hour and a half, and thereafter there should be a re-examination. That would be half of that time, so 45 minutes. This is what we have agreed. May we go back to private session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. N. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just -- the 45 minutes is with reference to me; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. N. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: May we go back to private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
